label: TMUA 2021 · Paper 1 · Question 17

hints.title: Rename the whole sine input
hints.body: Let u=x2+y2. First solve the sine equation as an equation in u, using its stated upper bound and the fact that a sum of real squares is nonnegative.
hints.recap: A two-variable expression may act as a single trigonometric input.
hints.pitfall: List both sine branches in every permitted cycle.
hints.pause: Find the allowed values of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math> without trying to solve separately for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: A two-variable expression may act as a single trigonometric input.

hints.title: Interpret each squared-distance value
hints.body: An equation x2+y2=c with c>0 is a circle centred at the origin with radius c. Apply this to each value you found.
hints.recap: The radius is the square root of the constant in a circle equation.
hints.pitfall: Equal changes in squared radius do not give equal changes in radius.
hints.pause: Convert the allowed constants into radii and arrange them from smallest to largest.

recall.reminder: The radius is the square root of the constant in a circle equation.

hints.title: Compare the radial gaps
hints.body: To compare the sketches, check the inner radii and the way neighbouring gaps change. You can bound a square root between nearby integers or half-integers by comparing their squares.
hints.recap: Simple square-root bounds can distinguish geometric spacing without a calculator.
hints.pitfall: Judge spacing from the radii, not directly from the list of sine inputs.
hints.pause: Use several estimated radii to decide which complete sketch matches the pattern.

recall.reminder: Simple square-root bounds can distinguish geometric spacing without a calculator.

solution:
1. Solve for the squared radius. Put u=x2+y2, so 0≤u≤8π. The solutions of sinu=12 are u=π6+2kπ and u=5π6+2kπ. The permitted integers are k=0,1,2,3, giving u=π6{1,5,13,17,25,29,37,41}.

2. Take square roots. These are eight circles centred at the origin. Their radii, in units of π/6, are 1,5,13,17,5,29,37,41.

3. Compare the spacing. Approximate radii in these common units are 1,2.24,3.61,4.12,5,5.39,6.08,6.40. The early gaps are relatively large; later circles come in closer pairs, with the gaps generally shrinking outward. There is no circle of radius zero.

These features identify sketch A. The decimal estimates are only for comparing the sketches; the exact squared-radius values determine the graph.
knowledgePattern: Solve a trigonometric equation for squared radius and distinguish concentric-circle spacing
